market_holds: Spot $40.11 at the 2026-11-17 close (Yahoo bars). The sealed baseline gives a front-expiry straddle of 14.05%, an event-implied move of 13.68% and skew of -3.3 vol points (upside paid). The stock is -4.3% over 5 days and -3.8% over 20, and 10.5% below its 52-week high. That weakness is the market's: QQQ fell about 10% from 10-28 to 11-17 and SHOP about 16% from 10-19, while GLBE was roughly flat (+1%), so it has held up well in a tech selloff. Q3 guide (2026-08-12): GMV $1.995-2.045B, which is +34% at the midpoint and +35% at the top against Q3-25 GMV of $1.512B, after +44% in Q2. Revenue guide is $308.5-315.5M and adj. EBITDA $58.5-62.5M. FY26 GMV guide is $8.81-9.11B, revenue $1.305-1.355B, EBITDA $278-300M, and the implied Q4 GMV is about +31.5% at the midpoint by my arithmetic. Consensus per the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-10: EPS $0.33 (whisper $0.35), revenue about $314.8M, near the top of the guide. The preview says the bar is a print above the top of the range plus another raise. Short interest is about 2.5% of float. In the last eight prints (open/close vs prior close), the stock closed up only twice despite beat-and-raise every time: Nov-24 +12/+12, Feb-25 -9/-18, May-25 -22/-19, Aug-25 +9/-9, Nov-25 -1/-4, Feb-26 +23/+17, May-26 -5/-9, Aug-26 +0.5/-0.8. The Aug-26 print beat the top of the GMV guide by 5.2% and the revenue top by 4.7%, but it came after a 22% run-up and the stock did nothing.
view: Global-E sets guidance that it then beats, and the market knows it. Q2 GMV came in 5.2% above the top of the guide, and the Q3 guide again assumes growth slows from 44% to about 34%. The independent read-through points to another beat, but not a large one. Shopify's Q3 (2026-11-03) showed international GMV slowing from 37% to 32% and total GMV from about 31% to 29%, with Europe +33% in constant currency. If Global-E slows by the same ~5 points, Q3 GMV is about $2.10B, roughly 3% above the top of the guide. That is about what a consensus already sitting at the top expects. FX was close to neutral for Q3: EUR/USD averaged 1.151 against 1.169 a year earlier and about 1.16 when the guide was set, and management had already said it assumed no FX tailwind in H2. The Q4 guide is the larger risk. EUR/USD averaged 1.120 in October and 1.116 so far in November (last 1.103 on 11-13), against about 1.16 in Q4-25 and at the August guide. A roughly 4% stronger dollar is a translation and demand headwind on non-USD cross-border spend, so the FY raise may not carry the whole Q3 beat. Luxury demand (LVMH +1% organic, fashion -5%, in Q3 2026) is soft but not new. Against that: the stock has held up through the tech selloff, short interest is low, and in Feb-26 a strong outlook took it up 17%. The line it trades on is the FY/Q4 GMV guide and organic growth ex-Passport. I can see reasons for a small downside lean (a reaction history that sells the news, a dollar headwind on the Q4 guide, Shopify's international slowdown) but none I can show the price fails to hold. The implied move is rich against a median close reaction of about 9-10%.

recommendation.reason: Global-E habitually beats a conservative guide, and both consensus and the preview already sit at or above the top of the range. The only fresh independent data (Shopify's international slowdown from 37% to 32%, and the dollar strengthening about 4% since the August guide) leans mildly against the Q4 guide. I cannot show that consensus fails to hold either factor. No mechanism clears 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 GMV well above $2.10B (around +40% or more) with an FY GMV raise to about $9.2B+ despite the stronger dollar would make this an up print. A Q4 implied guide below about 30% growth, or a cut to take rate or gross margin, would make it a clear down print.

questions_pursued.answer: The Q2 actual beat the top of the guide by 5.2%. The Q3 guide implies +34% after +44%, so a beat is the base case. Consensus revenue already sits at the top of the range.

self_critique: Every guide since early 2025 has been beaten at the top. The Q3 guide again builds in a 10-point slowdown, larger than the 5-point slowdown the Shopify data suggests. In Feb-26 a strong outlook drove a 17% gain. The stock's resilience through the tech selloff may reflect buyers positioning for the beat rather than a crowded long. The FX argument depends on management guiding at spot, and on the Q4 consensus not already including the stronger dollar, which I could not check. The negative reaction history is partly from 2025, when tariffs were the issue, so it may not carry forward. All of this pulls back toward 50, which is where I already am.
